'''Guido Torrigiani''' (13 January 1920 – 7 June 2000) was an Italian mathematician, computer scientist and politician. A member of the [[Italian Socialist Party]], he served as president of the [[Province of Livorno]] from 1956 to 1964 and later played a significant role in the development of academic computing at the [[University of Pisa]].<ref name="morto">{{cite news |title=È morto Torrigiani, matematico e uomo politico. Era stato docente all'Università di Pisa e presidente della Provincia |work=[[Il Tirreno]] |date=8 June 2000}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sba.unipi.it/sites/default/files/persona_archivio/per_guido_torrigiani.pdf |title=Per Guido Torrigiani |publisher=Sistema Bibliotecario di Ateneo, University of Pisa |access-date=4 June 2026 |format=PDF}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Born in [[Porto Santo Stefano]], Torrigiani studied at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore]] in [[Pisa]], graduating in mathematics in 1942.<ref name="80anni">{{cite news |title=Fra supermatematica e politica: gli 80 anni del prof. Torrigiani |work=Il Tirreno |date=15 January 2000}}</ref><ref name="biografia">{{cite news |title=La biografia: a 17 anni entrò alla scuola Normale |work=Il Tirreno |date=8 June 2000}}</ref> After initially joining the [[Action Party (Italy)|Action Party]], he became a member of the [[Italian Socialist Party]] following the former's dissolution.<ref name="80anni" /><ref name="biografia" />

Torrigiani settled in [[Livorno]] and taught [[mathematical analysis]] at the [[Italian Naval Academy]].<ref name="80anni" /><ref name="biografia" /> In 1956 he was elected [[president of the Province of Livorno]] and was subsequently re-elected for a second term.<ref name="morto" /><ref>{{cite book |url=http://mizar.comune.livorno.it/statistica/download/pubblicazioni/ER/VitaDemocratica_1946_2001.pdf |title=La vita democratica a Livorno. I risultati del voto in città dalla Liberazione ad oggi |publisher=Comune di Livorno |location=Livorno |year=2003 |page=106 |archive-date=2019-04-24 |access-date=2026-06-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190424100110/http://mizar.comune.livorno.it/statistica/download/pubblicazioni/ER/VitaDemocratica_1946_2001.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

During the 1960s, he was invited by his friend [[Alessandro Faedo]] to help establish the [[Centro Nazionale Universitario di Calcolo Elettronico]] (CNUCE), one of Italy's pioneering computing research centres. Torrigiani later served as its director until 1979.<ref name="80anni" /><ref name="biografia" /> He also taught mathematical analysis in the engineering faculty of the [[University of Pisa]] and conducted research at the Department of Applied Mathematics "Ulisse Dini".<ref name="morto" /><ref name="80anni" /><ref>{{cite news |title=Il Torrigiani scienziato e la sua battaglia per una scuola moderna |work=Il Tirreno |date=12 June 2000}}</ref>

From 1975 to 1990 he served as president of the Pietro Mascagni Institute of Musical Studies in Livorno, promoting musical and concert activities in the city.<ref name="80anni" /><ref name="biografia" /><ref>{{cite news |title=In memoria del prof. Torrigiani. Istituto Mascagni, concerto per ricordare l'ex presidente |work=Il Tirreno |date=15 June 2001}}</ref>

He died in Pisa on 7 June 2000 following a cardiac arrest.<ref name="morto" /><ref name="biografia" /> Among the tributes paid after his death was a message from Italian president [[Carlo Azeglio Ciampi]], a personal friend.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ciampi ricorda il prof. Guido Torrigiani. "Ha dedicato le sue energie alla formazione di generazioni di allievi" |work=Il Tirreno |date=8 June 2000}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.iltirreno.it/livorno/cronaca/2010/06/09/news/guido-torrigiani-ricordato-in-provincia-1.1905698 |title=Guido Torrigiani ricordato in Provincia |work=Il Tirreno |date=9 June 2010 |access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref>
